content.text: Section 11 covers all preferred elements; section 10 contains no undercutting fee-conditionality or early deletion.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position in full: (a) up to six months of transition assistance on Customer's request, including knowledge transfer, migration and continued service at existing scope and service levels — priced at the expiring Order Form rates, which is better for us than "then-current rates"; (b) return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, expressly not withholdable over a fee dispute; and (c) secure deletion from active systems and backups after Customer confirms successful return, with written officer certification and a narrow, use-restricted legal-retention carve-out. Cross-checking sec-10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination), nothing undercuts this: access ends only after the agreed transition period, Customer Data rights survive, and there is no fee-conditionality or early destruction. No redline warranted.
